title: Mother of drug war victims set to observe Duterte's ICC proceedings in The Hague
summary: The mother of two drug war victims is set to observe former President Rodrigo Duterte"s trial proceedings at the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague, Netherlands.

blocks.text: The mother of two drug war victims is set to observe former President Rodrigo Duterte’s trial proceedings at the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague, Netherlands.
In a "24 Oras" report from Oscar Oida on Thursday, members of the group Rise Up supported Llore Pasco, who embarked on a flight to The Hague.

As an observer, Pasco represents the parents of slain drug war victims who could not afford to attend the hearings in The Netherlands. She lost two sons to the drug war on the same day in 2017: Juan Carlos Lozano and Crisanto Lozano.

“Sobrang importante po dahil yung iba po hanggang ngayon ay takot pa rin at sabi ko nga palagi dahil tayo ang naiwan, tayo yung buhay, sino pa ang magtatanggol sa kanila? Sino pa ang magboboses kundi tayong mga buhay,” Pasco said.
(It's very important because the others are still afraid and I always say that because we are the ones left, we are the living, who else will defend them? Who else will speak up but us, the living?)
Pasco brings with her the bag of one of her children. She prayed for strength as her fight for justice continues.
Rise Up covered the expense of Pasco’s trip to the Hague. Members made contributions so that she could make the trip, signifying that they were serious about justice.

“Yung aming paglalakbay, kasama ang pamilya ng biktima, ay talagang napakahaba, mahirap, masalimuot… Pero nang makita namin ang determinasyon ng mga pamilya, lalo na yung mga nanay, yung mga nawalan ng anak, yung mga nawalan ng asawa, yung kanilang determinasyon. Sabi nga ng isang nanay, ‘alam ko dapat may hustisya pero di ko alam kung paano’,” Rise Up Coordinator Rubylin Litaw said.

(Our journey, together with the family of the victims, is so long, difficult, complicated... But when we saw the determination of the families, especially the mothers who lost their children, who lost their husbands, their determination. One of the mothers said ‘I know that there should be justice, but I do not know how to attain it.) — Jean Mangaluz/BAP, GMA News
